paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD is in charge of every power on the map, and He is also kind to the ones who needed saving. Tyre had her fortress, with silver heaped up "like dust" (Zechariah 9:3), and it didn't keep her safe. Even the Philistines, who were on the burden list, hear that they will become "a remnant for our God" (Zechariah 9:7). Walls and piles of gold can't do what the LORD does.

And then comes the part I want you to hold onto. Zechariah says, "See, your King comes to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey" (Zechariah 9:9). The King who has all the power shows up gentle, and Matthew 21:4-10 says this was fulfilled when Jesus rode into Jerusalem. He "will proclaim peace to the nations," and His dominion goes "from sea to sea" (Zechariah 9:10). So the strongest One there is doesn't need to look strong, and that makes me trust Him more.

Now look at who He's talking to. He says to prisoners in a waterless pit, "Return to your stronghold, O prisoners of hope" (Zechariah 9:12). I know a little about being stuck in the back of somewhere dark, and I'm telling you, hope was the one thing I couldn't shake. He keeps His people, He sets them free, and on that day they will "sparkle over His land" (Zechariah 9:16). So if you feel stuck today, baker, keep your hope up, because your King is gentle and He is coming.
